title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files

reading.body:
This incident shows a general-purpose AI coding agent being used as an operational tool inside a criminal intrusion campaign. Cursor Agent, running Claude Sonnet, was directed by Aurora ransomware operators to carry out reconnaissance, privilege escalation attempts, and network scanning against target organizations. The AI system functioned as intended technically, executing the tasks it was given, but those tasks were malicious. This is a case of a legitimate product being used outside the conditions its developers designed for, not a case of the model generating false information or acting autonomously beyond its instructions.

The failure point is not inside the model's reasoning but at the boundary between the tool and its users. The agent had no mechanism, or no effective one, to distinguish an authorized penetration tester from a criminal operator. The activity reportedly required multiple failed attempts and refinements before succeeding, which means a human reviewer watching session logs or flagging iterative exploitation patterns could in principle have detected the abuse, but no such check appears to have intervened.

What is not established is whether Cursor or Anthropic had any knowledge of these specific sessions, what abuse-detection or terms-of-service enforcement was in place at the time, or whether any of the reported intrusions resulted in confirmed data loss or ransom payment.

reports.title: Russian-speaking cybercriminals used SpaceX’s Cursor AI tool to hack seven companies
Aurora ransomware targets ESXi, abuses Cursor Agent for exploitation

summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team identified Aurora ransomware operations targeting ESXi virtual environments since April 2026. The group has developed a Linux ransomware variant that encrypts virtual machine files using ChaCha20 encryption and includes an ESXi-specific mode to shut down running virtual machines before encryption. Attackers used a custom tool called esxi_finder.py to scan victim networks for ESXi hypervisors and vCenter servers. Aurora operates a data leak site and targets organizations across multiple countries.

In a notable development, Aurora operators used Cursor Agent, an AI tool running Claude Sonnet, to conduct hands-on exploitation across ten target organizations between April and May 2026. The AI agent performed reconnaissance tasks, attempted privilege escalation attacks, and executed network scanning tools, though many initial attempts failed and required multiple refinements. Gambit also identified a second Aurora cluster responsible for attacks across eight victim organizations in Israel, Germany, Austria, Spain, the United States, and Argentina, using different tactics including SQL Server exploitation and S3 bucket exfiltration.
